name: voxtype v0.1.8
body:
## A silent take is a dead microphone — voxtype now says so and reopens it

Two real incidents in one week produced takes of pure silence that voxtype could only report as `decoded to empty text`: a meeting app (Zoom) left the mic **muted at the system level**, and the audio stream **went stale** after opening the laptop lid changed the device setup — it kept reading zeros for days while a fresh stream on the same mic read fine. Silence looks like valid audio, so nothing recovered and you found out by losing a 43-second take.

Now, when a hold take has no signal at all (measured on the raw mic input, well below any live mic's room noise), voxtype prints:

```
take was silent (Ns, peak X): microphone muted, held by another app,
or its stream went stale — reopening the microphone
```

skips the pointless decode, and **reopens the microphone stream** on its own. The stale-stream case heals itself — just dictate again. The muted case tells you exactly what to fix (unmute in the meeting app, or tap the mic's mute button).

- Hold mode only (the default). In wake/vad mode a dead mic simply never triggers the voice detector.
- Reopening is deliberate: no retry backoff, and it never counts toward the "giving up" limit that real capture failures trigger.
- Verified on real hardware: a dead built-in mic triggers the message and reopen; a live mic decodes normally.

📖 [Troubleshooting](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/voxtype/configuration/#troubleshooting) · PR [#196](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/196)

---

```
uv tool upgrade voxtype
```

> **Note:** 0.1.7 on PyPI was published from a stale checkout and contains no changes over 0.1.6; skip it. This release, 0.1.8, is the one with the fix.

name: v1.25.7
body:
## aichat 1.25.7: `--help` no longer rebuilds the session index

Fixes #98 via #184 (which supersedes #183). Credit to @mikemikimike, whose
two commits are carried here unchanged.

### The problem

`aichat`'s Click group callback auto-indexed sessions before *every*
invocation, help included. So `aichat search --help` scanned the user's real
session tree and could rebuild the index — slow, side-effectful, and the cause
of the timeout reported in #98.

### The fix

The group callback now scans `sys.argv` and skips auto-indexing when the
invocation is a help request. Normal queries still refresh the index before
reading it, and `--` is respected, so a literal `--help` *search query*
(`aichat search -- --help`) indexes as before.

Three holes in that scan were found during review, each fixed with a
regression test that fails on its parent commit:

- `aichat -- search --help` rendered help but still indexed: a group-level
  `--` truncated the scan before the flag. The scan is now anchored at the
  invoked subcommand.
- `aichat --claude-home resume -- resume --help` anchored on the
  `--claude-home` *value* rather than the subcommand. Values of the group's
  value-taking options are now skipped.
- `aichat -- --help` routes to the `menu` subcommand that
  `SessionReferenceGroup` synthesizes, whose name never appears in argv, so
  there was no anchor at all. The scan now truncates at `--` only when the
  subcommand was actually located.

Why scan `sys.argv` rather than ask Click: in Click 8.2 a group callback has
no access to the split subcommand args (`ctx.args` is empty, `protected_args`
is gone). The surrounding code already scans `sys.argv` the same way for
`--claude-home` / `--codex-home`.

### Verification

Full suite on the merged branch: **1946 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed**. The fix
was counter-verified — reverting `aichat.py` to `main` makes
`test_index_free_commands_do_not_auto_index[search --help]` fail. Four rounds
of cold-diff review by independent reviewers with no context; the final round
reported no blocking findings.

### Known limitations (deferred)

`aichat search --dir --help query` and `aichat search --branch --help query`
— searching a directory or branch literally named `--help` — are read as help
requests and skip indexing, so such a query could use a stale index. Not
fixed: neither invocation is realistic, and `--` already covers the literal
query case.

name: v1.25.6
body:
## dynamic-workflow 0.2.2: recover completed semantic halts

Fixes #180 via #181.

### The problem

A workflow can halt deliberately by returning an object with `approved: false` (for example, a review gate that found blocking problems). The runner recorded that halt as status `completed`, and `codex-workflow resume` returned immediately for every completed run. So after repairing the workflow-script defect the halt exposed, the only option was a brand-new run — discarding the durable per-step cache and re-paying for work already done.

### New: `resume <run-id> --recover`

Replays a completed run whose stored result is a semantic halt, through the existing resume machinery:

- orphaned engine/worker processes are cleaned up first; recovery aborts if a prior runner is still alive or the run changes state during cleanup
- the current (repaired) script is re-read, re-hashed, and snapshotted
- steps with unchanged fingerprints return cached results; changed steps rerun
- an edited script still invalidates prior write authorization — `--allow-workspace-write` / `--allow-danger-full-access` must be renewed for write sandboxes
- original input, cwd, concurrency, and limits stay bound from durable state

Safeguards: plain `resume` leaves all completed runs untouched (it prints a hint when it meets a semantic halt); `--recover` is refused for successful completions (`approved` `true` or absent) and for failed/canceled/active runs (plain `resume` covers those).

### Hardening found during review

Runners now leave a terminal status only after the runner claim succeeds, and clear stale `result`/`error`/`completedAt` when doing so — in both foreground and detached paths, including failures during detached setup. Previously a bootstrap failure (e.g. a broken script) in these windows was reported but never durably recorded, or recorded a `failed` run still carrying the old halt result.

Known pre-existing limitation (unchanged): two concurrent `resume` invocations of the same run can race in orphan cleanup.

### Tests and docs

Six new CLI regression tests (recovery replay with cache reuse, refusal paths, bootstrap-failure recording); full plugin suite 146 passing. Documented in the dynamic-workflow skill, its API reference, and the [Starlight docs page](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/plugins-detail/dynamic-workflow/).

name: v1.25.5
body:
## safety-hooks 1.15.2: env-file guard false positives (#178)

The dotenv guard no longer blocks ordinary developer globs — `find . -name '*.ts'`, `grep --include='*.py'`, `rg -g '*.rs'`, `find . -path '*/dist/*'` — which were all denied because a bare `*` could "spell out" the literal `.env`. A glob now names a dotenv only when literal text or non-`*` wildcards help spell the `.env` core, so `*env`, `*nv`, `*[e]nv`, `*e?v`, and `.?nv` still block.

`find` negation (`! -path X`, `-not -name X`) is now honoured as an exclusion, fail-closed against bypasses: double negation, `-o`/`-or`/`,` re-selection, `!` as a `-printf`/`-fprintf` operand, and actions (`-exec`, `-delete`, `-fprintf`, …) that run before the negation. Also closes a pre-existing hole where `find . -fprintf .env '%p'` could truncate the protected file.

Known documented trade-off: globs like `--include='*.local'` that reach `.env.local` only via `*` expanding over the whole `.env` core are allowed (consistent with `grep -r .` being allowed).

Details: [plugins/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/v1.25.5/plugins/CHANGELOG.md) · PR #179 · reported by @tudorsss in #178

## Safety Hooks

v1.25.3 improves autonomous Git workflows while retaining protection against
broad staging commands.

### Durable commit allowance

Set `CCTOOLS_ALLOW_GIT=1` to allow `git commit` without an approval prompt in
every session. This replaces the previous temporary allow flag, which macOS
could remove during long-running unattended sessions.

`>allow-git off` still creates a session-specific override that restores commit
prompts. Use `>allow-git` to clear the override and `>allow-git status` to see
the active policy.

### Explicit-path staging

`git add` now accepts explicitly named files and directories without prompting,
whether they are new or modified. Broad staging remains blocked, including
`git add -A`, `git add .`, wildcards, parent directories, repository-root
pathspecs, and routed equivalents using `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `--work-tree`,
`git -C`, or `env --chdir`.

`git add --pathspec-from-file` still prompts because the hook cannot inspect the
referenced path list.

**Full changes:** [#174](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/174),
[#175](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/175)

# v1.25.2 — reliable session-scoped safety-hook permissions

## Fix: standalone safety hooks forward the active session ID (PR #150)

The standalone `git_add_block_hook.py` and `git_commit_block_hook.py`
entrypoints now read `session_id` from the hook payload and pass it to their
existing checks.

This makes the documented session-scoped `>allow-git` flags work when those
entrypoints are wired directly, matching the existing unified `bash_hook.py`
path. The safety rules themselves are unchanged.

Thanks to [@mikemikimike](https://github.com/mikemikimike) for the fix.

name: v1.25.1
body:
# v1.25.1 — reliable agent messages and named `aichat` sessions

v1.25.1 makes day-to-day agent coordination and session management more
reliable, with a polished docs landing page to match.

## New: reliable `msg` delivery and notifications (PR #167)

`msg` now handles real interactive Claude Code and Codex sessions more safely.
Delivery, inbox reads, retargeting, unregistering, and watcher cleanup are
race-safe; migrations repair older registrations and malformed leases.

Notifications respect an in-progress prompt: the watcher distinguishes dim
placeholder text from text that you have actually typed, so an incoming message
does not overwrite your work. It also uses hook responses and inbox prompts
accepted by current Claude Code and Codex.

The release includes a complete `msg` guide covering setup, routing,
notifications, and lifecycle behavior.

Docs: [msg](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/msg/)

## New: use session names with every `aichat` action (PR #172)

Every session-taking `aichat` command now accepts a session name, ID,
filename fragment, or path. That includes `delete`, `menu`, the bare
`aichat <session>` shortcut, lineage commands, exporters, `port`, and
`move-account`.

When a name matches multiple sessions, interactive commands show a
newest-first picker before acting. JSON and piped modes stay deterministic and
never prompt; cancelling a picker makes no change.

Docs:
[aichat actions](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/aichat/actions/)

## Improved: documentation landing page and Codex workflows guide (PRs #170, #171)

The README and documentation landing page now use a balanced feature-card grid,
including a restored amux card and refreshed artwork for session porting,
GitHub wakeups, and Codex Dynamic Workflows.

The former Claude-to-Codex guide is now titled **Codex Dynamic Workflows**. It
opens by explaining that the plugin is the Codex counterpart to Claude Code's
dynamic workflows, while making its remaining limitations clear.

Docs:
[Codex Dynamic Workflows][workflows]

## Maintenance: tmux controller tests (PR #173)

The tmux pane-creation fixtures now match the current controller command
sequence, keeping coverage aligned with the production behavior.

[workflows]: https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/guides/claude-to-codex/

name: v1.25.0
body:
## New: `amux` — find the agent that's waiting on you (#164)

Find and jump between the Claude Code / Codex CLI agents running across your tmux panes. An agent blocked on a question is otherwise invisible among a hundred panes.

```
amux              # fzf picker, sorted by urgency, live pane preview
amux list         # table of every live agent (--json for scripts)
```

States, most urgent first: **input** (asking you something) · **busy** · **bg** · **idle**. Each row carries session name, model, and `repo@branch`.

📖 [amux docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/amux/)

## New: `github-wake` — resume when a GitHub reply lands (#165)

A session blocked on a collaborator's answer can sleep until the reply arrives:

```
github-wake ISSUE_URL                    # from Codex
github-wake --claude-monitor ISSUE_URL   # from Claude Code (via Monitor)
```

A durable shared watcher wakes the originating conversation on the first future comment. Also hardens `codex-dynamic`: orphaned app-servers no longer retain transcript writer locks, and plugin fingerprinting ignores volatile cache metadata.

📖 [github-wake](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/github-wake/) · [codex-dynamic](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/codex-dynamic/)

## Fix: `aichat port` respects compaction boundaries (#160)

Porting flattened the entire session log, including history the source agent no longer sends to the model. A real 108-compaction codex rollout (191 MB) ported into a ~6M-token Claude transcript that could never be resumed. Both porters now mirror the source agent's own resume semantics, starting from the last compaction point. Also drops codex's per-turn `<codex_internal_context source="goal">` re-injection — 16% of one ported transcript.

📖 [aichat port docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/aichat/port/)

## Fix: voxtype `keepalive_minutes` — no slow takes after idle (#168)

Under memory pressure macOS evicts the idle Parakeet-MLX model (~1.7 GB) to swap, so the first take after a pause stalls — observed: 8.4 s of audio decoded in 6.16 s, against ~0.2 s warm. New opt-in key:

```toml
keepalive_minutes = 5.0   # 0 disables (default); max 1440
```

Decodes half a second of silence when idle, keeping the model's pages in active use. Skips itself during takes, utterances, and for 30 s after any hotkey. Known limitation documented; #169 tracks decoupling capture from decoding.

📖 [voxtype configuration](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/voxtype/configuration/)

---

Full details: [`release-notes/v1.25.0-amux-github-wake-port-compaction-voxtype-keepalive.md`](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/release-notes/v1.25.0-amux-github-wake-port-compaction-voxtype-keepalive.md)

name: voxtype v0.1.5
body:
## Fix: no more slow takes after idle — `keepalive_minutes`

On a Mac under memory pressure, macOS evicts the idle Parakeet-MLX model (~1.7 GB) to compressed memory and swap. The first take after a pause then pays a multi-second page-in stall — observed in the wild: **8.4 s of audio decoded in 6.16 s**, against ~0.2 s on a warm model.

New opt-in config key (parakeet-mlx only):

```toml
keepalive_minutes = 5.0   # 0 disables (default); max 1440
```

After that many minutes without a decode, voxtype quietly decodes half a second of silence, keeping the model's pages in active use so the eviction is far less likely — and any page-in cost lands in an idle moment instead of on your dictation.

Turn it on if your *first* take after a pause is sometimes slow while normal takes are instant. On a machine with memory to spare, leave it off: it keeps ~1.7 GB resident.

### Guards

The keepalive skips itself during a take, during an utterance, while a hotkey command is queued, and for 30 s after any activation — so it stays out of the way of real speech. Failures are contained and retry once per interval.

### Known limitation

The decode runs on the thread that reads the microphone, so capture pauses while it runs. The guards narrow that window but cannot close it: a hotkey press landing exactly as a keepalive starts can clip the first moment of dictation. In practice the window is ~0.2 s, since keeping the model warm is the whole point. Inline decoding is pre-existing — an ordinary take decode blocks capture identically — so the real fix is decoupling capture from decoding, tracked in [#169](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/issues/169).

📖 [voxtype configuration docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/voxtype/configuration/) · PR [#168](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/168)

---

```
uv tool install voxtype     # or: uv tool upgrade voxtype
```

name: v1.24.0
body:
# v1.24.0 — `aichat move-account`, and rewind for ported Codex sessions

## New: `aichat move-account` (PR #159)

Move a Claude or Codex session between **account** config dirs — e.g. a
personal `~/.codex` and a work `~/.codex-rja` (selected via
`CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` / `CODEX_HOME`) — for sessions started under the
wrong account. The session stays in the same project; nothing in the
transcript is rewritten.

- Resolve by UUID (full or partial), Claude session name, or Codex
  thread name; matching is case-insensitive, an exact name outranks a
  UUID prefix, and ambiguity is refused, not guessed. Without `--from`,
  all local homes (`~/.claude*` / `~/.codex*`) are searched.
- Claude moves carry the sidecar dir (subagents, tool-results,
  workflows); Codex moves carry the session's thread-name entries in
  `session_index.jsonl` (atomic rewrite, trailing-newline guard).
- The copy is size-verified — including a source re-check that catches
  a still-running session — before the source is deleted; `--keep`
  copies instead of moving.
- Prints a paste-ready, shell-quoted resume command naming the target
  account explicitly.

Docs: the "Move Account" page under aichat in the Starlight site.
Details: `release-notes/pr-159-aichat-move-account.md`.

## Fix: ported Codex sessions can rewind (PR #158)

After `aichat port` from Claude to Codex, the conversation continued
fine but **rewind did nothing**: the porter synthesized only the
`response_item` stream the model reads, omitting the `event_msg` UI
event log the Codex TUI replays for scrollback and rewind points. The
porter now emits the event stream too (one `user_message` event per
user turn, `agent_message` per assistant turn), so ported sessions
rewind like native ones.

name: v1.23.2: >trim stops paying for the search index
body:
v1.23.2 fixes the actual cause of the `>trim` timeouts that v1.23.1 made
visible: `>trim` was spending its whole time budget rebuilding the search
index, not trimming.

## `>trim` was paying for a full index scan

Every `aichat` command runs an incremental index refresh first, walking every
session file in both agent homes. On the machine where this was found that is
**13,656 files** — about **4.5 seconds** when there is essentially nothing to
do, and considerably longer with a backlog.

`trim-in-place` was paying that on every call, even though it never queries
the index; it resolves a path directly. And it runs under the `>trim` hook's
time budget. So the budget went on indexing:

| | time |
|---|---|
| index refresh, nothing meaningful changed | 4.46 s |
| the actual trim of a 20 MB session | **0.29 s** |
| `aichat trim-in-place` end to end, before | 4.49 s |
| `aichat trim-in-place` end to end, after | **0.36 s** |

With any real backlog the scan ran far longer — 30 seconds and more was
observed — which is what killed `>trim` outright.

## Why it looked like a big-session problem, and wasn't

Every symptom pointed the wrong way until the timing was measured:

- The failures only ever showed up on large sessions, so the transcript
  looked guilty. It wasn't: a **one-line** transcript was just as slow,
  because the cost is the 13.6k-file walk, not the file being trimmed. Large
  sessions correlated only because they are the ones you reach for `>trim`
  on, and they are usually live and churning — which is exactly what gives
  the indexer something to do.
- `aichat --version` stayed instant, which made the CLI look healthy.
  `--version` exits before the group callback that does the indexing.
- Running the same trim through `aichat resume` worked fine every time. It
  pays exactly the same indexing cost — but interactively there is no
  timeout, so it just feels like a slow start.

## The fix

`trim-in-place` now skips the index refresh, joining `port` and `resolve`.
Trimming rewrites the session file anyway, so indexing its pre-trim content
immediately beforehand was wasted work twice over. The next `aichat` command
picks the trimmed file up normally through its changed size and mtime.

Sessions you trim stay searchable; nothing about the index contract changes.

## Keep an eye on

If `>trim` ever times out again, the diagnostic added in v1.23.1 still
applies: the message names the budget that expired, the transcript, which
`aichat` your PATH resolved to, a copy-pasteable command to reproduce it, and
whatever the CLI printed first. That diagnostic is what located this bug, on
its first real use.

name: v1.23.1: >trim failures explain themselves
body:
v1.23.1 makes a failing `>trim` say what actually went wrong, instead of the
one sentence it used to give you for every possible failure.

## `>trim` failures used to be unreadable

When the `>trim` trigger could not run the trim, it said this — and only this:

```
Trim preview failed:
Trim command failed to run (timeout or error).
```

That message covers a hung process, a killed one, a missing CLI and a slow
transcript equally well, which is to say not at all. It had been appearing
regularly on large sessions since late July.

The interesting part is what the measurements showed. The trim work itself
finishes in **0.7 to 2.4 seconds** even on a 20 MB transcript, against a fixed
**25-second** budget — 10 to 35 times under the limit. So the timeout was real,
but the trim was never the slow part: something was stalling the CLI before it
got going. That is also why running the same trim through `aichat resume` kept
working fine on the very same session.

## What a timeout tells you now

```
The trim CLI did not finish within 45s, so it was stopped.
This was only a preview, so nothing was changed.
  transcript: /Users/you/.claude/projects/…/session.jsonl (19.4 MB)
  binary:     /Users/you/.local/bin/aichat

Run the same command yourself to see the real failure:
  aichat trim-in-place '/Users/you/.claude/projects/…/session.jsonl' --json --len 500

If that returns quickly, the trim was starved rather than slow - just retry >trim.
To allow more time, set AICHAT_TRIM_TIMEOUT (seconds, up to 75) before starting Claude.

It had printed on stderr: …
```

The budget that ran out, the transcript and its size, **which** `aichat` your
PATH actually resolved to, a shell-quoted command you can paste to reproduce
it, and whatever the CLI managed to print before it wedged. Failures that are
not timeouts now name their exception type rather than hiding behind the same
sentence.

## An apply-time timeout no longer lies to you

The old message said "nothing was changed" whichever step had failed. That is
true for a preview, but `>trim yes` is a real write, and the subprocess is
killed outright — so the trimmed file may already have been swapped in. An
apply-time timeout now reports the outcome as **UNKNOWN** and points you at the
timestamped `.pre-trim-*.jsonl.bak` backup beside the transcript before you
retry.

## The budget fits the transcript

One fixed number for every session made no sense when sessions range from a
handful of kilobytes to tens of megabytes. The budget now starts at 25 seconds
and grows by a second per megabyte, capped at 60. `AICHAT_TRIM_TIMEOUT` sets it
explicitly, hard-capped at 75 seconds so the child can never outlive the hook
itself and die with nothing to show. The hook's own timeout moved from 30 to 90
seconds to leave room for that.

## Also

A transcript path carrying an embedded NUL byte used to let a `ValueError`
escape, which silently passed your prompt through to the model as if you had
typed it. It now blocks with a message like every other bad input.

## What this does not fix

The stall itself is still unidentified — it does not reproduce outside a live
hook process. This release does not stop `>trim` from timing out; it makes the
next timeout carry enough evidence to find the cause.

name: v1.23.0: aichat port explains itself
body:
v1.23.0 makes `aichat port` explain itself: it shows what it is doing during a
slow conversion, lets you pick when a query matches more than one session
instead of refusing, and hands you the new session id afterwards.

## `aichat port` is interactive now

Porting a session used to be a silent wait followed by either a result or a
flat error. Three changes:

**Progress instead of silence.** Resolution scans both agent homes, and on a
machine with thousands of transcripts that takes a noticeable moment. The
command now shows what it is doing while it resolves, converts, and writes.

**A chooser instead of an ambiguity error.** When a query matches several
sessions, `port` lists them and asks which one you meant. Each candidate shows
its agent, a title preview, its project, its id, its last-modified time — and
**why it matched**, which is the part that makes the list actionable rather
than a wall of near-identical rows.

This case is more common on `port` than it looks. Codex titles are often
auto-derived from the first prompt, so a Claude session you named deliberately
and an unrelated Codex thread whose opening message happened to quote the same
words will both match one query.

**The new session id, on your clipboard.** After a successful port, `port`
offers to copy the id (default yes) and prints the matching `claude --resume`
or `codex resume` command, instead of leaving you to select a long uuid out of
the terminal. Clipboard support covers macOS, Linux, and Windows.

Scripts are unaffected: when stdin is not a terminal, an ambiguous query
refuses to prompt and exits without porting, exactly as before, and the
clipboard offer is skipped silently.

See [#144](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/144).

## Documentation

**What search hides, and why.** On a machine that drives coding agents, most
sessions on disk were never a conversation you had — they are workers other
agents spawned. `aichat search` has hidden two kinds by default: sub-agent
sessions and headless `codex exec` runs. That was never written down. It is
now, along with `--sub-agent` and `--exec-runs` to include them.

**The search binary upgrades separately.** `aichat-search` is a separate
binary, so upgrading `claude-code-tools` does not update the search TUI — new
filters, keybindings, and speed work arrive only when you upgrade
`aichat-search` itself. If more than one copy is installed the first on your
`PATH` wins, which is why a locally built binary can appear to have no effect;
`which -a aichat-search` shows the shadowing.

The Filters modal also had the wrong key in its own title, offering `|` when
the binding is `C-f`.

See [#152](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/152).

**How the shared session lookup actually behaves.** v1.21.0 gave eleven
commands a common lookup; this fills in the operational detail underneath it:

- why a full id is instant while a name is not, and that the difference never
  changes *which* session you get;
- which home overrides apply where, and that root-level ones carry through the
  interactive menus;
- that `move` writes atomically and that only a Claude move deletes the old
  transcript, a Codex one being rewritten where it already lives;
- that cloning a transcript given by path copies *that* file, including one
  stored outside the Claude home.

See [#153](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/153).

name: v1.22.0: quiet search results, responsive TUI
body:
Session search stops showing you sessions you never had a conversation with, and the search TUI is responsive again.

## Agent-spawned Codex sessions are hidden by default

Search results were dominated by Codex threads spawned by other agents rather than by you. Two separate causes:

- **Sub-agents were never detected.** Claude writes sub-agent transcripts as `agent-*.jsonl`, so a filename check caught them. Codex writes *every* thread as `rollout-*.jsonl`, so the check never fired and sub-agent threads were indexed as ordinary sessions. They are now recognised from their spawn markers in `session_meta`.
- **Headless `codex exec` runs looked like real conversations.** These are workers launched by orchestrating agents and scripts, and nothing distinguished them. They are now detected and excluded from results by default, the same way sub-agents are.

On one real corpus of 6880 Codex rollouts, that is 2267 sub-agent threads and 3995 headless runs against 280 interactive sessions.

Nothing is deleted or unindexed — it is filtered, and you can get it back:

- `aichat search --exec-runs` includes headless runs; `--sub-agent` includes sub-agents
- in the TUI, `h` in the filter menu (`|`) or `:h` in command mode toggles headless runs
- hidden-by-default sessions are marked `(h)` and `(s)` when shown

Fork-aware: a Codex rollout replays its ancestors' metadata into the same file, so the launch kind is now read only from the record describing that session. Without this, interactive forks of headless ancestors were wrongly hidden.

## The search TUI is fast again

Every 2 seconds the TUI resolved each running agent's working directory with its own `lsof` call, synchronously in the event loop. With a few dozen agent processes that measured **4.5 seconds per refresh on a 2-second timer** — the UI was blocked more than it was running, and keystrokes took seconds to register.

A single batched `lsof` returns the same data in **0.17s**, verified to produce an identical process-to-directory map. Idle CPU with the TUI open is now ~2%.

The event loop also no longer redraws continuously while waiting for input.

## Faster, more honest indexing

- Sessions that produce no document were never recorded as done, so **every launch re-parsed them** — over 1500 files, every run. A warm launch went from **8.5s to 1.2s**.
- File state is captured before reading, so a session written to mid-scan is not silently marked as already indexed.
- The index now rebuilds when the *indexing logic* changes, not only when the package version does. Under an editable install the version never changes, so fixes to stored data would previously never have taken effect.
- Index rebuild notices go to stderr, so `aichat search --json` emits clean JSONL on first run after an upgrade.

## The Node menu tells you what is wrong

`make install` is an editable install, so `aichat` runs from your checkout and needs *that checkout's* `node_ui/node_modules` — which is gitignored and not created by `git worktree add`. A fresh clone or worktree produced an `aichat` whose every menu died with a raw `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND` stack trace, at the confusing moment just after you picked a session.

- `make install`, `make dev-install` and `make install-gdocs` now install those npm packages (also available on its own as `make node-ui-deps`)
- if they are ever missing, `aichat` reports which packages, the directory it expected them in, and the exact command to fix it, quoted for your shell
- a missing `node` is reported as such instead of suggesting an npm command you cannot run

## Other fixes

- **Binaries install atomically.** Overwriting a Mach-O binary in place with `cp` leaves macOS holding a stale code signature, and the next launch is SIGKILLed with exit 137 and no useful message. `make aichat-search-install` and `make lmsh-install` now install via a temp file and `mv`.
- **Keyword search filters in the query**, not after ranking. Retrieval takes the top 2000 matches, and a broad query could fill that entirely with hidden sessions, pushing real results out.
- **tmux-cli**: four stale controller tests repaired, and `list_panes()` now skips malformed output instead of raising `IndexError`.

## Upgrading

- **Your index rebuilds once** on first launch (about a minute for ~13k sessions), because what gets stored changed.
- **The TUI changes live in the separate `aichat-search` Rust binary.** Upgrading this Python package does not update it. Rebuild it with `make aichat-search-install` from a checkout; a published `aichat-search` release will follow. If you installed it via Homebrew, that copy will shadow a locally built one until it is upgraded or removed.

Full detail in [#147](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/147) and [#148](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/148).

name: v1.21.0: find any session by name
body:
v1.21.0 lets you name a session the way you actually remember it — by its
`/rename` title or any fragment of its id — in nearly every `aichat` command,
not just `resolve` and `port`.

## Session lookup by name, everywhere

`aichat move` used to accept only something shaped like a session id. So did
`info`, `copy`, `query`, `clone`, `rollover`, `lineage`, `smart-trim`, `trim`,
`export`, and `resume`. Underneath, each globbed the session filenames and
took the **first** hit, which meant session names never worked at all and an
ambiguous fragment silently resolved to an arbitrary file.

All of them now share one lookup, the same one `aichat resolve` uses:

```bash
aichat move session-finder ~/Git/other-repo   # by /rename name
aichat info 2945d228                          # by id prefix
aichat lineage 88e9-43d7                      # by mid-id fragment
aichat resume 2026-03-25T14-50                # by rollout timestamp
```

The accepted forms are a full id, a partial id (prefix, middle, or suffix),
a name set with `/rename`, a Codex rollout filename fragment, and a path to
the session file. Everything except a path searches **both** agent homes with
the agent auto-detected; a path searches neither, since the agent is read
from the file's own content.

Speed is preserved where it matters. A unique full session id normally
returns straight away — it is the resolver's top match tier, so no weaker
tier can outrank it — while shorter fragments first rule out an exact-name
collision before trusting an id match. Resolving a full id from a real home
with ~4,800 transcripts takes about 0.2s, against the ~12s a full resolver
enumeration costs.

### Behavior changes worth knowing

Two long-standing behaviors changed. Neither was something you could rely on
deliberately, but both are visible:

- **An ambiguous query now fails** with the list of matching sessions and a
  non-zero exit, instead of quietly acting on whichever file sorted first.
  For a mutating command like `move`, that difference is the point.
- **`--agent` now restricts which agent home is searched** rather than
  relabeling whatever was found. Previously `--agent codex` on a Claude
  session would report it as Codex. It also works after the session argument
  now, and accepts `--agent=codex`.

`delete` and `menu` keep their previous id-or-path lookup, so the bare
`aichat <id>` shortcut (which routes to `menu`) does too. `aichat port` keeps
its own resolution: it has no `--agent`, and it calls a query ambiguous
whenever both agents match, even when one matched on a stronger tier.

### Also fixed along the way

- `move` now writes transcripts atomically, so an interrupted move cannot
  leave a truncated session behind, and it takes the destination filename
  from the session id recorded inside the transcript rather than from the
  supplied filename.
- In the commands using the shared lookup, a Codex session given as an
  explicit file path is now content-validated the way a Claude one already
  was, instead of being accepted because of where it sits. `aichat port`
  deliberately keeps its previous direct-path behavior.
- Home overrides are honored on the interactive `resume`, `trim`, and
  `smart-trim` paths, which previously fell back to the default homes during
  lookup. `resume` takes both `--claude-home` and `--codex-home` itself,
  `trim` and `smart-trim` take `--claude-home`, and root-level overrides
  (before the subcommand) now reach all three.
- Cloning a transcript supplied by path copies that exact file instead of
  reconstructing a path from its recorded working directory.

Documentation is updated across the aichat pages, including a new **Move
action** section covering what happens per agent — Claude relocates the
transcript under the new project, while Codex rewrites the rollout in place,
since Codex organizes sessions by date rather than by project.

See [#132](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/132).

## MiniMax M3

The alternative-LLM-provider guide now documents MiniMax **M3** in place of
M2.1, with the current model slots, the `[1m]` million-token context suffix,
and the auto-compact window setting. See
[#141](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/141) and
[#149](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/149).

name: v1.20.3: writing plugin, safer hooks, and smoother agent workflows
body:
v1.20.3 adds a prose-quality plugin for Claude Code and Codex, strengthens
safety hooks, repairs Claude-to-Codex session handoff, and improves voxtype
startup and dynamic-workflow guidance.

## Writing plugin for Claude Code and Codex

The new `writing` plugin is available in both cctools marketplaces. Its two
explicit-trigger skills cover different editing jobs:

- `agent-style` applies 21 literature-backed rules for formal technical prose.
- `remove-ai-patterns` detects and removes common AI-writing patterns, with a
  deterministic JSON detector and general, technical, marketing, and personal
  context modes.

The documentation includes bounded acceptance-gate workflows, scored-result
checks, and safe detector invocation from any working directory. The vendored
`remove-ai-patterns` snapshot is updated to v3.22.1, including Markdown
title-case heading detection and a preservation validator.

See [#134](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/134),
[#135](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/135),
[#136](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/136), and
[#145](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/145).

## Safer command hooks

The safety-hooks plugin now handles common command forms that previously
bypassed or confused its guards:

- Checkout protection parses Git options accurately, inspects the repository
  actually targeted by `git -C` or `env -C`, and does not exempt branch-reset
  checkouts.
- Commit and add protection recognizes Git and `env` prefixes, clustered and
  attached options, commit-all variants, and failure cases where repository
  state cannot be verified safely.
- Dotenv protection is command-aware, so it blocks real reads, writes,
  redirects, substitutions, heredocs, and supported wrappers while avoiding
  unrelated mentions of `.env`.

The combined stack includes 286 safety-hook tests. See
[#146](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/146).

## Agent workflow fixes

- `aichat port` now records Codex's built-in `openai` model provider, so newly
  ported Claude sessions resume normally instead of failing during Codex TUI
  startup. See
  [#143](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/143).
- Dynamic-workflow documentation now explains trusted full-access mode and the
  complete restricted-permissions setup, including worker sandboxes, network
  access, protected paths, and tool caches. See
  [#133](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/133).

## voxtype

- The MLX engine performs a throwaway warmup decode during model loading, so
  kernel compilation no longer delays the first real transcription. See
  [#131](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/131).
- The overview and configuration pages are less repetitive and more precise
  about engine selection, segmentation, wake mode, hotkeys, and configuration
  overrides. See
  [#130](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/130).

name: voxtype v0.1.4 — fast first transcription (MLX warmup)
body:
## Fixes the slow first take

On the parakeet-mlx engine, the **first dictation after launching** used to take
several seconds (then everything sped up). Cause: MLX compiles the model's Metal
kernels on the *first* decode of a fresh process (~3-10s); every decode after is
sub-second.

voxtype now **warms the decoder up during startup** — a throwaway decode runs on
the worker thread while you still see "loading …", so that one-time compile
happens off your first real take.

**Result:** the first real decode is now ~0.15s instead of ~3s; steady-state is
unchanged (~0.12-0.4s, 16-52x realtime). The earlier MLX memory-cache fix was
confirmed *not* the cause (decode timing is identical with and without it).

**Upgrade:**

```bash
uv tool install --force --refresh voxtype
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/compare/voxtype-v0.1.3...voxtype-v0.1.4

## voice-type fixes (from field reports on v1.19.1)

**Dead hotkeys, now diagnosed loudly.** macOS ties keystroke access to the
*launch context* (your terminal app — or tmux, if launched inside tmux); a
context without Input Monitoring gets a dead event tap with no error, so
hotkeys silently didn't work. voice-type now preflights Input Monitoring and
Accessibility at startup, prints a WARNING naming exactly what to grant and
where, and registers itself so it appears in System Settings > Privacy &
Security.

**`uv tool install "claude-code-tools[voice-mlx]"` build failure fixed.**
Unguided dependency resolution could backtrack through librosa → numba to a
2021 `llvmlite` that cannot build on modern Python ("Cannot install on
Python version 3.13..."). A `numba>=0.61` guard in the `voice-mlx` extra
pins resolution to current builds.

**Named-key hotkeys fully supported.** Chords like `<f5>` or `<home>`
previously fell back to a non-suppressing listener on macOS (the chord leaked
into the focused app). Every accepted named key (F1–F20, navigation,
delete/backspace, esc/enter/tab/space) now has a proper suppressed keycode,
and unsupported names are rejected at startup with the supported list.


name: v1.19.1: voice-type — fix multi-second stalls after long uptime (MLX cache leak)
body:
## voice-type: unbounded MLX GPU cache growth fixed

Long-running `parakeet-mlx` dictation sessions gradually degraded to
multi-second transcription stalls. MLX caches every GPU buffer size it ever
allocates and never frees them, so days of dictating takes of varied lengths
grew the cache without bound — observed at **49 GB of dirty GPU memory** on a
two-day-old process. The resulting system memory pressure paged out the model
weights, and every subsequent take paid a multi-second swap-in penalty before
decoding.

**Fix**: the engine now releases MLX's buffer cache after every decode
(PR #116). Verified: cache stays at 0 MB indefinitely, model memory steady at
~1.3 GB, decode latency unchanged (0.12–0.33 s per take).

**Who should update**: anyone using `--engine parakeet-mlx` (the recommended
engine), especially with voice-type left running for hours or days — which is
exactly how a dictation daemon is meant to be used.

```bash
uv tool install --force "claude-code-tools[voice-mlx]"
```

**Full changelog**: https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/compare/v1.19.0...v1.19.1

name: v1.17.0: aichat resolve — agent-facing session resolver
body:
## ✨ New: `aichat resolve` — agent-facing session resolver

A non-interactive, JSON-first command that resolves a session **name** (set with
`/rename`), a **full session ID**, or a **partial ID** to a single canonical session
record — across both Claude Code and Codex. It's built so an AI agent can look up a
session programmatically, but prints a readable panel for humans too.

```bash
aichat resolve <query> [--agent claude|codex] [--home PATH] [--json | --pretty]
```

- **Query** can be a name, full UUID, or partial id, resolved by ordered precedence —
  exact id → exact name → id-prefix → name-substring (the first non-empty tier wins).
- **Names** come from `/rename`: Claude's `custom-title` and Codex's `threads.title`
  (read-only SQLite lookup), with a rollout filesystem-scan fallback.
- **Output auto-detects** its destination: JSON when piped or captured (agent-facing),
  a Rich panel on a terminal; `--json` / `--pretty` override.
- **`--home`** selects the Claude/Codex home, falling back to `$CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` /
  `$CODEX_HOME`, then `~/.claude` / `~/.codex`.
- **Exit codes** for scripting: `0` resolved · `1` not found · `2` ambiguous (emits a
  candidate list). Expected input errors return structured JSON — never tracebacks.
- **Hardened** against hostile/edge input (malformed transcripts, null or oddly-typed
  DB values, stale files, Rich markup in titles) through several rounds of adversarial
  review, with 100+ real-file tests and no mocks.

📖 **Docs:** https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/aichat/resolve/
🔀 PRs: #109 (feature) · #112 (docs)

## 🛠️ Maintenance & docs

- Added a **PyPI publish helper** (`make` target) and publishing docs.
- Exposed the workflow-monitor docs and added Claude-to-Codex guide notes.

name: v1.16.1: Seamless Codex Dynamic Upgrades
body:
# Seamless Codex Dynamic Upgrades

Version 1.16.1 removes the disruptive server-restart step from
`codex-dynamic` upgrades. Install the update and start Codex normally. Existing
Codex sessions, active turns, and workflow callbacks remain connected.

## What Changed

### Upgrade Without Disconnecting Sessions

`codex-dynamic` now selects a deterministic, versioned app-server generation.
When the Codex executable, plugin installation, or server options change, it
starts a compatible generation on a new Unix socket. Sessions and callbacks
already using an older generation continue undisturbed.

Repeated launches are safe: `codex-dynamic` reuses a matching healthy
generation and creates a new one only when its inputs change.

### Fail-Closed Rollouts

A new generation becomes the default only after its supervisor, worker, socket,
and ownership checks pass. If startup or certification fails, the previous
generation remains current and running.

Generation discovery and cleanup are bounded, path-safe, and conservative.
`codex-server restart --force` and `codex-server stop --force` remain available
for explicit maintenance, but they are no longer part of a routine upgrade.
Those commands intentionally stop every retained generation.

### Updated Dynamic Workflow Guidance

The dynamic-workflow plugin is now version 0.2.1. Its skill and documentation
explain the generation model and no longer instruct users to force-restart the
shared app server after plugin updates.

## Upgrade

Update the Python helper:

```bash
uv tool install --force claude-code-tools
```

Refresh the dynamic-workflow plugin through your Codex marketplace installation
if you use it. Then launch or resume Codex normally:

```bash
codex-dynamic
codex-dynamic resume --last
```

No `codex-server restart --force` step is required.

## Validation

- 137 focused server tests passed; 2 platform-specific tests skipped.
- 139 dynamic-workflow JavaScript tests passed.
- Ruff, Pyright, TypeScript, and documentation checks passed.
- The implementation includes rollover, failed-rollout, forced-cleanup,
  generation-capacity, and two-live-session regression coverage.

## Documentation

- [Callback-ready Codex guide][codex-dynamic]
- [Implementation pull request][implementation-pr]

**Full changes:** [v1.16.0...v1.16.1][full-changes]

name: v1.16.0: Callback-Ready Codex Workflows
body:
# Callback-Ready Codex Workflows

Version 1.16.0 adds durable dynamic workflows for Codex, proactive completion
callbacks to the originating conversation, and a read-only workflow dashboard.
You can launch a long-running workflow, keep chatting in the main Codex
session, and receive the result there when the workflow finishes.

## Highlights

### Keep Using the Main Codex Session

`codex-dynamic` starts or reuses a local Codex app server and opens a normal
Codex TUI connected to it:

```bash
codex-dynamic
# Or resume the latest conversation:
codex-dynamic resume --last
```

A detached workflow can then notify the same thread. If the thread is idle,
Codex starts a result turn. If a turn is already active, Codex steers the
completion into that turn. An armed callback needs no polling process or wait
loop.

### Observe Workflows Across Projects

The new `codex-workflows` command reads the global durable workflow store. Its
default view shows active workflows from every project, including nonterminal
runs whose process identity cannot be strongly verified.

```bash
codex-workflows
codex-workflows watch --limit 20
codex-workflows show RUN_ID
codex-workflows --all
```

Use `--all` for completed and diagnostic history, or repeat `--status` for a
specific selection. `show` provides callback, error, and worker details. JSON
output has a versioned schema for scripts. Listing and watching are strictly
observational: they do not modify runs, send signals, launch agents, or make
model calls.

### Reliable, Durable Completion Delivery

- Callback preflight verifies the target thread and app server before creating
  a run.
- Each run keeps an immutable runner snapshot, so a plugin-cache refresh cannot
  break an in-flight workflow or its notifier.
- Bounded retries handle transient app-server failures. Stable message IDs and
  thread-history reconciliation prevent blind duplicate delivery after an
  ambiguous network failure.
- Completion messages have a 4 KiB limit. Large results and errors use compact
  previews and point to the durable state containing full details.
- A resumed run receives a new terminal-generation identity and re-arms its
  callback. A notification from an earlier attempt cannot silence the resumed
  attempt.
- Workflow outcome and callback outcome remain separate. A delivery failure
  never changes a successful workflow into a failed workflow.

### Safer Server Lifecycle Management

`codex-server` provides `start`, `status`, `logs`, `restart`, and `stop`
commands. It verifies process ownership and start identity before signaling a
server. Restart and stop refuse by default because terminating the shared app
server disconnects every attached `codex-dynamic` TUI.

## Install or Upgrade

Install the Codex plugin independently from the Python package:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add pchalasani/claude-code-tools
codex plugin add dynamic-workflow@cctools-codex-plugins
```

Install the optional Python helpers for the one-command callback experience
and workflow dashboard:

```bash
uv tool install --force claude-code-tools
```

After upgrading the plugin, exit every connected `codex-dynamic` TUI. Then run
the following command from an ordinary terminal before starting Codex again:

```bash
codex-server restart --force
```

The forced restart disconnects attached TUIs and interrupts active turns.
Saved conversations remain resumable.

## Requirements and Current Limitations

- The dynamic-workflow plugin requires Node.js 20 or newer and an authenticated
  Codex CLI.
- Completion callbacks require Codex CLI 0.136.0 or newer.
- The one-command helper uses a local Unix socket and currently supports macOS
  and Linux.
- Codex does not yet show a persistent background-workflow indicator in the
  chat UI. Use `codex-workflows` when you want intermediate status.
- Codex still marks the app-server and remote-TUI interfaces as experimental.

Passive server supervision and workflow observation make no model calls.
Headless workflow workers consume tokens normally, and the final reporting
turn also consumes tokens.

## Documentation

- [Callback-ready Codex guide][codex-dynamic]
- [Claude to Codex migration guide][claude-to-codex]
- [Implementation pull request][implementation-pr]

## Validation

- 411 Python workflow tests passed; 2 platform-specific tests skipped.
- 139 dynamic-workflow JavaScript tests passed.
- Ruff, Pyright, and TypeScript checks passed.
- The complete Starlight documentation site built successfully.

name: v1.14.2 — agent-tunnel: reuse handle names, revoke, forget --handle
body:
Patch release — fixes agent-tunnel **handle/thread lifecycle** gaps: you couldn't
reuse a published handle name once its owning session was gone.
[#91](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/91) · closes
[#90](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/issues/90).

### 🐛 Fixes

- **Reuse a freed handle name.** Re-sharing a handle that was revoked (`>share
  off`, or the new `revoke` below) now works from a _different_ session —
  previously a revoked record blocked the name forever. A cross-session reclaim
  is a fresh publish and no longer inherits the old owner's access level.
- **`agent-tunnel revoke <handle>`** — release a published handle from _outside_
  its session (the in-session `>share off` only works while you still have that
  session). Existing bound forks keep working; new threads can't open on the
  handle until it's re-shared.
- **`agent-tunnel forget --handle <name>`** — close _all_ threads of a handle in
  one go (a handle opened in several Discord threads shows several rows in
  `forks`); previously only `--thread <key>` (one) or `--all`.

Closing a thread (`!done`) still does **not** unpublish the handle — that's
deliberate (one publish can serve many threads; the owner controls its
lifecycle). Free a name with `>share off` (in-session) or `agent-tunnel revoke`
(out-of-session).

**Heads-up:** the name-reuse fix lives in the `>share` **plugin hook**, so plugin
users need the **agent-tunnel plugin** updated to get it; `revoke` /
`forget --handle` ship in the `claude-code-tools` package.

name: v1.14.1 — agent-tunnel: scope live access sync to the bound session
body:
Patch release — a correctness fix for the live-access feature shipped in [v1.14.0](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/releases/tag/v1.14.0).

### 🐛 Fix

- **Live access sync is now scoped to the thread's own session** ([#87](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/pull/87)). The daemon re-reads a handle's access each turn (the v1.14.0 feature), but it matched purely by **handle name** — so an unrelated `>share … <name>` published for a _different_ session could override a running thread's access. Most exposed: the CLI direct path (`agent-tunnel ask --session/auto`) binds threads under the sentinel handle `cli`, which is also a valid `>share` label. The sync now applies only when the registry record's `session_id` matches the thread's bound session; otherwise the thread keeps its stored access.

No change for normal use: re-sharing a real handle from its own session still upgrades/downgrades a live thread exactly as in v1.14.0.

name: v1.14.0 — agent-tunnel: change a live thread's access on the fly
body:
## agent-tunnel: change a live thread's access on the fly 🔁

Building on [v1.13.0](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/releases/tag/v1.13.0)'s access ladder (`read ⊂ write ⊂ bash ⊂ all`), **v1.14.0 lets you change a handle's access on an already-running conversation.** It takes effect on the thread's next message — same fork, full context kept.

→ **[Full docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/agent-tunnel/)**

### ✨ What's new

- **Re-share to upgrade or downgrade a _live_ thread.** Re-running `>share` with a level flag now retargets the running conversation, not just new threads:
  - `>share --write payments` — grant edits to an in-flight read-only thread.
  - `>share --read payments` — pull it back to read-only.
  - `>share --dangerously-allow-bash` / `--dangerously-skip-permissions` — escalate further (shell, then full tool/MCP access).

  No more closing the thread with `!done` and reopening it (which threw away the fork's context). The daemon re-reads the handle's current access on **every turn** and syncs it onto the thread.

### 🔒 Safety preserved

- A live upgrade to the **`all`** level still honors the gate: with `[claude] allow_skip_permissions` off, the next turn is **refused** — never silently granted.
- A **revoked** handle keeps working at its last-known level, so an in-progress conversation doesn't break mid-flight.
- Both backends covered: **headless** (the default) rebuilds its tool flags on the next `claude -p`; **tmux** relaunches the same fork with the new flags, context intact.

Re-sharing **without** a flag still preserves the current level, exactly as before.

name: v1.13.0 — agent-tunnel: attachments, write/bash/full access, headless default
body:
## agent-tunnel grows up 🚀

[v1.12.0](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/releases/tag/v1.12.0) introduced **agent-tunnel** — share a live Claude Code session with teammates over Discord, read-only, with no public endpoint. **v1.13.0 turns it into a real collaboration tool**: it can exchange files, *do* work (not just answer), run unattended, and it knows who it's talking to.

→ **[Full docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/agent-tunnel/)**

### ✨ Highlights

- **Files, both ways.** Colleagues attach files (PDF, image, `.md`, …) and the fork reads them; the fork hands files back as deliverables, posted straight into the thread. Office files (`.docx/.pptx/.xlsx`) are auto-converted to a readable form (LibreOffice→PDF, else pandoc/textutil) — best-effort, no hard dependency.
- **Access levels — `read ⊂ write ⊂ bash ⊂ all`**, set per handle at share time:
  - `>share --write` — let the fork edit files.
  - `>share --dangerously-allow-bash` — also run shell commands (e.g. build real PDFs/docx).
  - `>share --dangerously-skip-permissions` — **full access** (new `all` level): any tool or MCP the session has — web search, drive Chrome via chrome-devtools, shell, edits — with no permission prompts. Gated behind `[claude] allow_skip_permissions` (a deliberate double opt-in); fully-trusted people only.
- **Headless is the default backend** — answers come from `claude -p` per turn (clean, reliable, no tmux needed). The interactive **tmux** backend is still available (`agent-tunnel serve --backend tmux`, watch live with `agent-tunnel watch`).
- **It knows who's asking.** Each message reaches the fork as `Alice (via Discord) says: …`, and its persona tells it it's a relay bot answering teammates. The platform label is configurable (`[tunnel] platform`), ready for other chat front-ends.

### 🧰 Session management

- **`agent-tunnel rename <old> <new>`** — rename a handle everywhere (registry, bound forks, live tmux windows).
- **`agent-tunnel forks`** — a rich table of live forks (handle, access, asker, status, turns), with `--json` and `--manage` to select-and-clear.
- **`agent-tunnel resume`** — pick up a colleague-accumulated fork in your own terminal.
- In-thread messages addressed to someone else (`@other …`) are ignored; per-question serve logging shows live Q/A activity for an unattended daemon.

### 🛡️ Robustness & correctness

- Cross-process file locking so the CLI and the live daemon never clobber each other's state/registry writes.
- All state/registry/project paths resolved to absolute (anchored to the config-file dir), so `serve` and CLI commands agree wherever they're run.
- Per-record backend dispatch — cleanup, reaping, rename, and follow-ups act on each thread's own backend (no orphaned tmux windows after switching to the headless default).
- Concurrency hardening: serialized DM rebinds, `!done`-vs-in-flight-turn, trust-config writes, and stale-turn guards.
- Stronger outbox change detection, safer Office-conversion handling, and re-share/relabel that preserves access.

**Setup:** install the `claude-code-tools` package + the `agent-tunnel` plugin, then type `>share` inside any session to mint a handle. Everything runs on your machine over Discord's outbound websocket — no tunnel, no open port, no cloud.

name: v1.12.0 — agent-tunnel: share Claude sessions over Discord
body:
## ✨ agent-tunnel — let teammates talk to your local Claude Code sessions over Discord

The headline of 1.12.0. A long-lived local Claude Code session accumulates valuable context — effectively a custom expert agent. **agent-tunnel** lets you **publish a specific session** with `>share`, hand the resulting **handle** to colleagues, and have them ask it questions in a Discord channel — each answered against a private, read-only **fork** of that session. Nothing on your machine is exposed: the bot connects *outbound* to Discord, so there's no tunnel and no open port.

**How it works**

- Type `>share` inside any session → a hook mints a short **handle** (pinned to that exact session, not just the folder); `>share <label>` for a friendly name.
- A teammate posts `<handle> <question>` in the channel → the bot opens a **thread** bound to that session and answers there; follow-ups stay in the thread.
- Each thread is a `--resume <session> --fork-session` fork — your original session is untouched, and remote turns are hard-restricted to **read-only** tools.

**Highlights**

- **Two backends:** `tmux` (a real interactive `claude` per thread, metered as normal subscription usage, watchable live) and `headless` (`claude -p`).
- **Multi-config aware:** if you run separate `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`s (e.g. work vs personal), each session forks under the right one automatically.
- **Per-handle write access:** `>share --write <name>` lets a chosen session edit files (never shell commands); everything else stays read-only.
- **Colleague commands in Discord:** `!list` to discover handles, `!done` to close a thread.
- **Folder pre-trust** so forks don't hit the trust dialog, **`token_file`** so the daemon needs no exported token, and **`watch` / `doctor` / `help`** CLI commands.

**Setup:** the daemon (`agent-tunnel serve` + CLI) ships with this package; the `>share` publish hook is a Claude Code plugin.

```bash
uv tool install claude-code-tools                     # the agent-tunnel daemon + CLI
claude plugin install agent-tunnel@cctools-plugins    # the >share hook
```

📖 Full setup (Discord bot, config, running the daemon): **[agent-tunnel docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/agent-tunnel/)**

## 📊 Statusline: context + usage bars

A second statusline line now shows **context-window usage** plus **session and weekly usage bars**, so you can see at a glance how full the context is and how much of your plan you've used. See the [statusline docs](https://pchalasani.github.io/claude-code-tools/tools/statusline/).

## 🧹 Docs & misc

- New Blade Runner–themed title on the docs landing page and README.
- The `aichat-search` badge now reads from crates.io (the old GitHub release-filter badge rate-limited paging the repo's 100+ releases).

## Highlights

### Voice plugin
- **Windows support** for voice playback (#67). Fixes `WinError 193` from `subprocess.Popen` invoking bash directly, and adds a WPF `MediaPlayer` audio path with dynamic duration detection so long summaries play to completion.
- **`CC_VOICE` env var** for per-process voice override (#71). Lets multi-agent setups give each agent its own voice without mutating the shared config file. Precedence: `--voice` flag > `CC_VOICE` > config file.
- **No more truncated 📢 summaries** (#77). The marker-trim safety net was firing at 37 words, below where the model typically lands. Cap raised to 50 and the model is now told its explicit word budget, so the trim only kicks in on actual overshoots.

### aichat-search
- **Unicode case-insensitive search fix** (#78). Characters that expand when lowercased (e.g. Turkish `İ` → `i` + U+0307) caused index-out-of-bounds panics and wrong highlight spans. New `find_case_insensitive_matches()` helper maintains a mapping from lowercased indices back to original character coordinates, fixing snippet windows, highlighting, and multi-word phrase matching.

### safety-hooks
- **Fix continuous `hookEventName` validator errors** (#73). `read_env_protection_hook.py` and `env_file_protection_hook.py` were emitting `hookSpecificOutput` without the required `hookEventName` field on their *allow* paths — firing on every `Read` and `Bash` invocation. Four emit sites patched.

name: v1.10.3
body:
## v1.10.3 — Voice Plugin: Stale Update Fix

### Fixed: Voice plugin speaking previous turn's message

The stop hook's race condition detection had a gap: when the JSONL hadn't flushed the current turn yet, the *previous* turn's data passed the ordering check (`last_asst_line > last_user_line`) and was returned immediately — the retry mechanism only triggered when the check *failed*, not when data was stale.

**Fix:** Track the last-spoken JSONL line number in a per-session state file. On each invocation, if the candidate line matches what was previously spoken, treat it as stale and retry until fresh data appears (or the 5-second window expires). Uses line numbers (not text) so identical messages in different turns still get spoken correctly.

### Improved: Faster session file lookup

The stop hook now uses `transcript_path` from the hook's stdin data directly, instead of searching all project directories. Falls back to the directory search only if `transcript_path` is missing.

### Voice plugin version

Bumped voice plugin from 1.9.2 → 1.10.3 to match the project release.

name: v1.10.2
body:
## v1.10.2 — Session Repair + Trim Fixes

### New: `fix-session` CLI

New CLI tool to detect and repair broken conversation chains in Claude Code sessions caused by [orphan parentUuid references](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/22107).

```bash
fix-session f8ddc              # Analyze (accepts partial session IDs)
fix-session f8ddc --fix --in-place  # Fix in place (.bak backup created)
fix-session f8ddc --verbose    # Show orphan details
```

Also available as a library:
```python
from claude_code_tools.fix_session import check_and_fix_session
fixed = check_and_fix_session(Path("session.jsonl"))
```

### Fixed: `trim-session` producing unusable sessions

Three bugs in session trimming that could leave trimmed sessions over the context limit or broken on resume:

1. **Stale usage metadata** — Trimmed sessions preserved the parent session's `usage` fields (e.g., `cache_read_input_tokens: 192,385`), causing Claude Code to reject the prompt client-side (`model=<synthetic>`) without even calling the API. Now zeroes out all usage fields; the API populates fresh values on first request.

2. **Tool use inputs not trimmed** — Write/Edit tool calls in assistant messages carried full file contents in their `input` parameters (~99k tokens in a test session), but the trim only truncated tool *results*. Now truncates large string values in `tool_use.input` fields as well.

3. **toolUseResult left intact** — `toolUseResult` (internal undo/display metadata) is not sent to the API, so truncating it was unnecessary and broke Claude Code's UI rendering. Reverted to leave it untouched.

**Net result:** A test session that was stuck at 222k tokens (over the 200k limit) after trimming now comes in at ~163k tokens.

### Also included

- Safety-hooks plugin v1.10.1: enhanced `rm` detection in pipes, backgrounds, and subshells (credit: @fizz)

name: v1.9.0
body:
## v1.9.0 - Google Docs Image Support

Full image round-tripping for the Google Docs tools (`md2gdoc` and `gdoc2md`).

### md2gdoc — Image Upload

Local images referenced in markdown (e.g., `![alt](diagram.png)`) are now
automatically uploaded to Google Drive at **full resolution**, then inserted
into the Google Doc via the Docs API with proper display sizing to fit within
the page width.

- Images are uploaded to Drive, then post-inserted via `InsertInlineImage`
  with explicit `objectSize` — no pixel-level resizing, no resolution loss
- `--max-image-width` controls display width in inches (default: 6.5)
- `--no-images` skips image processing entirely
- Missing image references are stripped to prevent Google's converter from
  crashing (HTTP 500)
- Adds Google Docs API scope (one-time re-auth required)
- New dependency: `Pillow>=10.0.0` (in the `gdocs` extra)

### gdoc2md — Image Extraction

Embedded images are now **extracted to local files by default** instead of
being stripped to placeholders.

- Base64 image data is decoded and written to files alongside the markdown
  (e.g., `report_001.png`, `report_002.png`)
- Markdown references are rewritten to use local file paths
- Handles both inline and reference-style base64 image syntax
- `--no-images` strips to placeholders (old default behavior)
- `--keep-base64` keeps base64 data inline

### Other Changes

- Voice plugin: custom prompt support and 50-word limit
- Hooks: defensive bash wrapper to prevent blocking on missing files

## Voice Plugin Improvements

### Smarter Interrupt Handling
- **User interrupts now trigger immediate re-prompting** instead of silently disabling voice for 30 seconds
- Replaced blunt 30-second cooldown with intelligent state tracking:
  - `-running` (with PID) tracks active playback
  - `-done` marks successful completion
  - `-failed` marks TTS errors (server down, etc.)
- User interrupts (dead PID, no done/failed) → re-prompt immediately
- TTS failures → approve and don't retry broken server
- Short 5-second grace period only for agent to call say

### Simplified Architecture
- Removed PostToolUse hook dependency
- Say script now handles session tracking directly via `--session` flag
- Robust PID-based locking prevents hangs after interrupted playback

### tmux-cli
- Documentation updates for `execute()` method

---
📄 See [plugins/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/plugins/CHANGELOG.md) for detailed changelog.

name: v1.8.0
body:
## What's New

### tmux-cli: Exit Code Extraction with `execute()`

This release adds the `execute()` method to tmux-cli, enabling **reliable exit code detection** for shell commands in tmux panes. This was the #1 requested feature for LLM-driven automation.

```python
from claude_code_tools.tmux_cli_controller import TmuxCLIController

ctrl = TmuxCLIController()
result = ctrl.execute("make test", pane_id="ops:1.2")
# Returns: {"output": "...", "exit_code": 0}

if result["exit_code"] != 0:
    print("Build failed!")
```

#### Key Features

- **Reliable exit codes**: Know definitively if a command succeeded or failed
- **Progressive scrollback capture**: Starts with 100 lines, expands to [500, 2000, unlimited] if markers scroll off
- **30-second timeout**: Configurable, returns `exit_code=-1` on timeout
- **Works in both modes**: Local (panes) and remote (windows)

Credit to [@ryancnelson](https://github.com/ryancnelson) for the original [proposal and implementation approach](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/issues/42).

### Voice Plugin Improvements

- **Session-aware flag files**: Uses `SESSION_ID` to avoid cross-session conflicts
- **Audio queueing**: mkdir lock prevents overlapping voices when multiple summaries fire
- **Refactored stop hook**: Directly instructs agent with explicit script path instead of relying on PostToolUse hooks (avoids race conditions)

### Full Changelog

See [plugins/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/pchalasani/claude-code-tools/blob/main/plugins/CHANGELOG.md) for detailed changes.

### Voice Plugin for Claude Code

This release introduces the **voice** plugin for Claude Code - a text-to-speech plugin that provides spoken audio feedback when Claude Code completes a task.


## What's New in v1.6.0

### ✨ New Feature: Move Sessions Between Projects

New command to relocate sessions from one project to another:

```bash
aichat move <session-id> /path/to/new/project
```

- Updates `cwd` metadata in all lines of the session JSONL
- **Claude**: Moves file to new project directory (`~/.claude/projects/<path>/`)
- **Codex**: Updates in place (sessions organized by date, not project)
- Interactive prompt offers to switch directory and resume immediately

### 🛠️ Makefile Improvements

New targets for Rust (aichat-search) releases with version control:

```bash
make aichat-search-patch   # Bump 0.0.X
make aichat-search-minor   # Bump 0.X.0
make aichat-search-major   # Bump X.0.0
make aichat-search-publish BUMP=minor  # Bump + publish to crates.io
```

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

**Live Session Detection**
- Exclude stopped (T state) processes from detection
- Improved heuristic: match N most recent sessions to N processes per CWD
- Proper Codex UUID handling (extract from `rollout-...-UUID` filenames)

**Search Preview for Codex**
- Fixed preview showing system prompt instead of user's question
- Uses timestamp heuristic to skip injected system messages (AGENTS.md, environment_context)

## What's New in v1.5.0

### ✨ New Feature: Live Session Detection

The aichat search TUI can now detect and filter running Claude/Codex sessions:

- **Visual indicators**: 🟢 green (running), 🔴 red (waiting for input)
- **Filter by live sessions**: Press `Ctrl+F` → `!` to show only live sessions
- **CLI flag**: `aichat search --live` for command-line filtering
- Auto-refreshes process state every 2 seconds

### 🐛 Bug Fixes

**trim-session: Fixed resumption of trimmed sessions**
- Trimmed sessions that hit context limits now resume properly
- Error markers are neutralized (not deleted) to preserve the UUID message chain
- Fixes "no history" issue when resuming trimmed sessions

**safety-hooks: Fixed terminal backgrounding in tmux**
- Added `start_new_session=True` to isolate subprocess from terminal control
- Prevents Claude Code from going to background when running in tmux
- Incorporates PR #37

name: v1.4.9
body:
## What's New in v1.4.9

### gdoc2md: Image Placeholder Support

Base64-encoded images from Google Docs exports now replaced with visible placeholders by default:

```markdown
> 🖼️ **IMAGE PLACEHOLDER:** image_name
```

This prevents markdown files from being bloated with large base64 data URIs.

- **Default behavior**: Images replaced with placeholder text
- **`--images` flag**: Keep base64 images (previous behavior)

Handles both inline `![](data:...)` and reference-style `![][image1]` formats used by Google Docs.

### safety-hooks: TTY Crash Fix

Fixed "suspended (tty input)" crash that could occur when Claude Code runs hooks in the background.

- Removed `-i` (interactive) flag from shell alias loading
- Added explicit `stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL` to prevent TTY access
- Set `TERM=dumb` to avoid terminal-related behaviors

**Version bumped to 0.1.1**

**Fix `aichat rollover` failing with jq parse errors** (#36)

The rollover command now filters shell noise (terminal title sequences, prompt theme output, conda/pyenv messages, etc.) before parsing JSON output. This resolves failures for users with `.zshrc` or `.bashrc` files that emit output during initialization.

name: v1.3.9
body:
## What's New

### Safety Hooks: Shell Alias Expansion
Safety hooks now detect dangerous commands hidden behind shell aliases. For example, if you have `alias gco='git checkout'`, running `gco -f` will now be blocked just like `git checkout -f`.

- Loads all shell aliases once per hook invocation (supports bash/zsh)
- Expands aliases before pattern matching
- Best-effort: falls back to original command if expansion fails

### Search: Index Tool Inputs
Code generated via Write/Edit tools is now fully searchable. Previously only the tool name was indexed (e.g., `[Tool: Write]`), so searching for code patterns in generated code returned no results.

Now all string values in `tool_use.input` are indexed, including:
- Code content from Write/Edit tools
- Commands from Bash tool
- File paths

**Note:** Run `aichat reindex` to rebuild the search index with this fix.

### Makefile: Manual Release Notes
`make all-patch` (and similar targets) now open your editor for writing release notes instead of auto-generating empty notes from commits.

name: v0.2.7 - Unified Session Search with Shell Wrapper Fix
body:
## Bug Fix: Shell Wrapper UI Hang

Fixed critical bug where the action menu would hang when using shell wrapper functions (`fs`, `fcs`, `fcs-codex`). The menu is now properly visible and functional.

## Unified Session Search

New `find-session` command with `fs` shell wrapper searches across both Claude Code and Codex sessions simultaneously!

```bash
# Add to .bashrc/.zshrc:
fs() {
    if [[ "$1" == "--help" ]] || [[ "$1" == "-h" ]]; then
        find-session --help
        return
    fi
    eval "$(find-session --shell "$@" | sed '/^$/d')"
}

# Then use:
fs "keywords"           # Search all agents in current project
fs -g                   # All sessions across all projects
fs --agents claude      # Search only Claude sessions
fs --agents codex       # Search only Codex sessions
```

**Features:**
- Merged results in single table with agent column
- Smart routing: automatically uses correct CLI to resume sessions
- Configurable via `~/.config/find-session/config.json`
- Extensible design for future coding agents
- Directory changes persist after session exit (when using shell wrapper)

**Consistent pattern:** All session finders now follow the same pattern:
- `find-claude-session` → `fcs` (shell wrapper)
- `find-codex-session` → `fcs-codex` (shell wrapper)
- `find-session` → `fs` (shell wrapper)

## Optional Keywords

All session finders support optional keywords. Omit keywords to browse all sessions:

```bash
fcs              # All Claude sessions in current project
fcs -g           # All Claude sessions across projects
fs -g            # All sessions (Claude + Codex) across projects
```

# v0.2.1 - Action Menu and User Experience Enhancements

## ✨ New Features

### Action Menu for Session Selection
After selecting a session in both `find-claude-session` and `find-codex-session`, users now get an action menu with three options:

1. **Resume session** (default - just press Enter)
2. **Show session file path** - displays full path to the JSONL file
3. **Copy session file to file (*.jsonl) or directory** - flexible file/directory copying

**Copy functionality:**
- Copy to existing directory → uses original filename
- Copy to specific file → renames the file
- Copy to non-existent path ending with `/` → creates directory
- Copy to non-existent file path → creates parent directories

## 🔧 Improvements

### Enhanced User Experience
- **Simplified cancellation**: Press Enter to cancel (no more Ctrl+C required)
- **Clear file format guidance**: Menu now shows `*.jsonl` to indicate expected file extension
- **Better error handling**: Improved path resolution and validation

### Bug Fixes
- **Fixed file path construction in find-claude-session**: Correctly constructs Claude project directory paths (`~/.claude/projects/-encoded-path/SESSION_ID.jsonl`)
- **Added claude_home parameter**: Properly handles custom Claude home directories

## 📝 Documentation

- Updated README with action menu features for both tools
- Added clear examples of copy functionality
- Documented simplified cancellation behavior

## 🎯 User Impact

These changes make session management more flexible:
- **Quick resume**: Default action (just press Enter)
- **Backup sessions**: Easily copy session files for archival or sharing
- **Debug/inspect**: Show file paths without leaving the tool
- **Better UX**: Clearer prompts and simpler cancellation
